title: Economic Importance of Dairying:
text:
Economic Importance of Dairying:

1. FOOD PRODUCTION
- Milk and dairy products are a vital source of nutrition for many people. In many countries around the globe milk and dairy products has become part of people's cultures and long traditions.

Top 5 largest milk producing countries (2024-2025)
1. India 211.7 Million metric tons
2. European Union 150.17 Million metric tons
3. United States 102.45 Million metric tons
4. China 41.63 Million metric tons
5. Russia 34.07 Million metric tons

2. TRADE
- The world dairy trade expanded over the years and has been primarily driven by growing demand in developing countries, as summarized in the following quote from an outlook report from the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO 2003),
"As incomes increase, demand for greater food variety grows. Demand for higher-value and quality foods such as meat, eggs and milk rises, compared with food of plant origin such as cereals. These changes in consumption, together with sizeable population growth, have led to large increases in the total demand for animal products in many developing countries, and this trend will continue."

Top 5 largest milk exporters (2024- 2025)
1. New Zealand: (20.7%)
2. Germany: (9.9%)
3. Netherlands: (9.4%)
4. United States: (7%)
5. Belgium: (6.9%)

Top 5 largest cheese exporters (2024)
1. Germany: US$6.7 billion (15% of total cheese exports)
2. Italy: $5.8 billion (13%)
3. Netherlands: $5.8 billion (12.8%)
4. France: $4.3 billion (9.5%)
5. United States: $2.5 billion (5.5%)

3. EMPLOYMENT - due to the high demand for dairy services, it opens a long list of job opportunities for local and overseas workers.
- Farm manager and farm assistants
- Milker
- General farm workers

facts: Dairying holds economic importance in food production, trade, and employment.
Milk and dairy products are a vital source of nutrition and part of long traditions and cultures across many countries.
India is the largest milk producing country (2024-2025) with 211.7 million metric tons.
The European Union is the second largest milk producer (2024-2025) with 150.17 million metric tons.
The United States ranks third in milk production (2024-2025) with 102.45 million metric tons.
China ranks fourth in milk production (2024-2025) with 41.63 million metric tons.
Russia ranks fifth in milk production (2024-2025) with 34.07 million metric tons.
World dairy trade expansion has been primarily driven by growing demand in developing countries due to rising incomes and population growth (FAO 2003).
New Zealand is the top milk exporter (2024-2025) accounting for 20.7% of exports.
Germany is the second largest milk exporter (2024-2025) with 9.9% of exports.
Netherlands is the third largest milk exporter (2024-2025) with 9.4% of exports.
The United States is the fourth largest milk exporter (2024-2025) with 7% of exports.
Belgium is the fifth largest milk exporter (2024-2025) with 6.9% of exports.
Germany is the top cheese exporter in 2024, exporting US$6.7 billion (15% of total cheese exports).
Italy ranks second in cheese exports (2024) with $5.8 billion (13%).
Netherlands ranks third in cheese exports (2024) with $5.8 billion (12.8%).
France ranks fourth in cheese exports (2024) with $4.3 billion (9.5%).
United States ranks fifth in cheese exports (2024) with $2.5 billion (5.5%).
Employment opportunities opened by dairy services for local and overseas workers include farm manager and farm assistants, milker, and general farm workers.
